audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with Psalm 40/Jeremiah/Habakkuk citation texture; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for shadow, once-for-all offering, access, mutual encouragement, severe warning, endurance.

verses.restored: For Law, having shadow of coming good things, not the very image of the matters, by the same sacrifices they offer continually year by year, is never able to complete those drawing near.

familiar.text: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.

modern.text: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship.

original.text: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων, κατʼ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε ⸀δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι·

verses.restored: Otherwise would they not have ceased being offered, because those serving, once cleansed, would no longer have consciousness of sins/misalignments?

familiar.text: For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.

modern.text: If it could, would not the offerings have ceased? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.

original.text: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι, διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ ⸀κεκαθαρισμένους;

verses.restored: But in these there is reminder of sins/misalignments year by year.

familiar.text: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.

modern.text: Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins,

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατʼ ἐνιαυτόν,

verses.restored: For it is impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.

modern.text: because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

original.text: ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας.

verses.restored: Therefore, entering into the world, he says: Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but body you prepared for me.

familiar.text: Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:

modern.text: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said: “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.

original.text: διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει· Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι·

verses.restored: In whole-burnt offerings and offerings concerning sin you did not delight.

familiar.text: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.

modern.text: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.

original.text: ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας.

verses.restored: Then I said: Look, I have come—in scroll of book it has been written concerning me—to do your will, O Divine.

familiar.text: Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.

modern.text: Then I said, ‘Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll: I have come to do Your will, O God.’”

original.text: τότε εἶπον· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω, ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου.

verses.restored: Saying above, Sacrifices and offerings and whole-burnt offerings and offerings concerning sin you did not desire nor delight in, which are offered according to Law,

familiar.text: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law;

modern.text: In the passage above He says, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You delight in them” (although they are offered according to the law).

original.text: ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι ⸂Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς⸃ καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ ⸀νόμον προσφέρονται,

verses.restored: then he said: Look, I have come to do your will. He takes away the first to establish the second.

familiar.text: Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.

modern.text: Then He adds, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first to establish the second.

original.text: τότε εἴρηκεν· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ⸀ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου· ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ.

verses.restored: In that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Messiah once for all.

familiar.text: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

modern.text: And by that will, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

original.text: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ⸀ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ.

verses.restored: And every priest stands daily serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which are never able to take away sins/misalignments,

familiar.text: And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:

modern.text: Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

original.text: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθʼ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας, αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας.

verses.restored: but this one, having offered one sacrifice concerning sins/misalignments into the continuous, sat down at right hand of the Divine,

familiar.text: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;

modern.text: But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.

original.text: ⸀οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: from then waiting until his enemies be placed as footstool of his feet.

familiar.text: From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.

modern.text: Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet,

original.text: τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: For by one offering he has completed into the continuous those being sanctified.

familiar.text: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

modern.text: because by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.

original.text: μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.

verses.restored: And the holy Spirit also witnesses to us; for after saying,

familiar.text: Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,

modern.text: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says:

original.text: μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, μετὰ γὰρ τὸ ⸀εἰρηκέναι·

verses.restored: This is the covenant that I will covenant with them after those days, says Lord: giving my laws upon their hearts, and upon their mind I will write them,

familiar.text: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;

modern.text: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”

original.text: Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει κύριος, διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν διάνοιαν⸃ αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς,

verses.restored: and their sins/misalignments and their lawlessnesses I will certainly remember no more.

familiar.text: And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.

modern.text: Then He adds: “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ ⸀μνησθήσομαι ἔτι·

verses.restored: Now where release/forgiveness of these is, there is no longer offering concerning sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.

modern.text: And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed. A Call to Persevere (Jude 1:17–23)

original.text: ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων, οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας.

verses.restored: Therefore, siblings, having boldness for entrance of the holy places in the blood/life of Jesus,

familiar.text: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,

modern.text: Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,

original.text: Ἔχοντες οὖν, ἀδελφοί, παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: which he inaugurated for us as new and living way through the veil, that is, his flesh,

familiar.text: By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;

modern.text: by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body,

original.text: ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: and having great priest over the house of the Divine,

familiar.text: And having an high priest over the house of God;

modern.text: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

original.text: καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: let us draw near with true heart in full assurance of trust, hearts sprinkled from harmful conscience and body washed with clean water.

familiar.text: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.

modern.text: let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

original.text: προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως, ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ·

verses.restored: Let us hold fast the confession of hope without wavering, for the One promising is trustworthy.

familiar.text: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)

modern.text: Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.

original.text: κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ, πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος·

verses.restored: And let us consider one another for stirring up love and beautiful/good works,

familiar.text: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:

modern.text: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.

original.text: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων,

verses.restored: not abandoning our gathering together, as custom for some, but encouraging, and so much more as you see the day drawing near.

familiar.text: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.

modern.text: Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

original.text: μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν, καθὼς ἔθος τισίν, ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν.

verses.restored: For if we willingly sin/misalign after receiving knowledge of truth, sacrifice concerning sins/misalignments no longer remains,

familiar.text: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,

modern.text: If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains,

original.text: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία,

verses.restored: but a fearful expectation of judgment and zeal of fire about to consume the opposing ones.

familiar.text: But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.

modern.text: but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.

original.text: φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους.

verses.restored: Someone setting aside Law of Moses dies without mercies on testimony of two or three witnesses.

familiar.text: He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

modern.text: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

original.text: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνῄσκει·

verses.restored: How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one trampling the Son of the Divine, considering common the blood/life of covenant in which one was sanctified, and insulting the Spirit of grace?

familiar.text: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?

modern.text: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

original.text: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας, καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.

verses.restored: For we know the One saying: Vengeance is mine; I will repay. And again: Lord will judge his people.

familiar.text: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.

modern.text: For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”

original.text: οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ⸀ἀνταποδώσω· καὶ πάλιν· ⸂Κρινεῖ κύριος⸃ τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Fearful it is to fall into hands of living Divine.

familiar.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

modern.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

original.text: φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας θεοῦ ζῶντος.

verses.restored: But remember the former days in which, having been enlightened, you endured great contest of sufferings,

familiar.text: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;

modern.text: Remember the early days that you were in the light. In those days, you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.

original.text: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας, ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων,

verses.restored: sometimes being publicly exposed to reproaches and pressures, sometimes becoming partners with those so treated.

familiar.text: Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.

modern.text: Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.

original.text: τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι, τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες·

verses.restored: For you had compassion on prisoners and accepted seizure of your possessions with joy, knowing yourselves to have a better and remaining possession.

familiar.text: For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.

modern.text: You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.

original.text: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς ⸀δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ⸀ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ⸀ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.

verses.restored: Therefore do not throw away your boldness, which has great reward.

familiar.text: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.

modern.text: So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.

original.text: μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἔχει ⸂μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν⸃,

verses.restored: For you have need of endurance, so that having done will of Divine you may receive the promise.

familiar.text: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.

modern.text: You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.

original.text: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν·

verses.restored: For yet a very little while, the coming one will come and will not delay.

familiar.text: For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.

modern.text: For, “In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.

original.text: ἔτι γὰρ μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει·

verses.restored: But my righteous/just one will live by trust; and if one draws back, my soul/life has no pleasure in that one.

familiar.text: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.

modern.text: But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός ⸀μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: But we are not of drawing back into ruin, but of trust into preserving of soul/life.

familiar.text: But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.

modern.text: But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν, ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς.

translation_notes: Psalm 40's body prepared language follows Greek textual tradition; Hebrew/Greek difference should be flagged in second pass.
Warning language is severe but ends with confidence: we are of trust into preserving life.
Gathering together is for mutual stirring of love and good works, not institutional control.
safety_note: Hebrews 10 warning passages must not be used to terrorize sensitive consciences or coerce attendance. The pastoral movement is access, confidence, mutual encouragement, endurance, and preservation of life.
